items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO SOCIAL SERVICES
ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.276

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to using supplemental
nutrition assistance program benefits to purchase online groceries and to the
state supplemental nutrition assistance program outreach program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8247

SPONSOR: KAMINSKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, in relation to using supple-
mental nutrition assistance program benefits to purchase online
groceries and to the state supplemental nutrition assistance program
outreach program

 
PURPOSE:

To codify the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program online purchas-
ing pilot program to ensure SNAP participants have safe and alternative
methods to access groceries.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the social service law to allow SNAP to use SNAP bene-
fits to purchase groceries from eligible online grocery retailers and to
have groceries delivered pursuant to federal laws and regulations. The
state will enter into agreements with any eligible retailer.

Section 2 amends the outreach program to include information about the
delivery option. Makes amendments to address the statutory change of
name for the SNAP benefits program.

Section 3 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) helps low-income
individuals, senior citizens, the disabled and others feed their fami-
lies. Millions of people in New York look to the SNAP program to address
the State's growing food insecurity crisis. However, many vulnerable
populations who depend on SNAP benefits are struggling to access food in
a safe manner. SNAP beneficiaries are now looking to grocery delivery
services as a safe and alternative option during the COVID-19 pandemic.

In 2019, the USDA launched a two-year SNAP pilot program in New York
State, which permits SNAP recipients to pay for and order their
groceries online with participating retailers. It is critical to codify
the participation in the pilot program and make the program permanent
after the pilot finishes. The legislation also ensures the state enters
into an agreement with any eligible grocery retailer, so the program can
serve as many participants as possible.

Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it is crucial to encourage individuals to
stay at home to prevent the spread of the virus. Yet, even with the stay
at home orders, there is still a lack of awareness about being able to
order groceries online with SNAP benefits. Therefore, the bill requires
the State's SNAP outreach program to now include information about the
SNAP Online Purchasing Pilot program and any subsequent programs.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediate.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 46 Chapter 342
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 8247-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the  social  services law, in relation to using
        supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits  to  purchase
        online groceries and to the state supplemental nutrition assist-
        ance program outreach program"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require the Office of Temporary and Disability Assist-
ance (OTDA) to enter into agreements with grocery store retailers and to
create  a plan to encourage and expand participation in the supplemental
nutrition assistance program  (SNAP)  online  purchasing  program  (OPP)
administered by the US Department of Agriculture (USDA).

  New Yorkers are currently experiencing food insecurity in dramatically
higher  numbers  than  ever  before  and  I strongly support the goal of
expanding the availability of  fresh  food  via  online  platforms  that
accept  SNAP  benefits. However, this bill has technical flaws that task
OTDA with duties that are not federally allowable under the current  OPP
structure.   The OPP is also a pilot program and although the state will
be a willing partner should the program become permanent, amendments are
needed to reflect the current temporal nature of the program. The Legis-
lature has agreed to pass legislation in the upcoming session to correct
these technical issues. On the basis of this agreement, I am pleased  to
sign this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Authorizes the use of supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits to purchase online groceries in accordance with federal laws and regulations and relates to the state supplemental nutrition assistance program outreach program.
